parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
Use the following data to calculate a value for the enthalpy change of solution of copper(II) chloride, $\text{CuCl}_2\text{(s)}$. You might find it helpful to construct an energy cycle.

enthalpy change of hydration of $\text{Cl}^- = -378\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
enthalpy change of hydration of $\text{Cu}^{2+} = -2099\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
lattice energy of $\text{CuCl}_2\text{(s)} = -2824\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
The enthalpy change of hydration of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ is $-1579\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

Use the *Data Booklet* to suggest why there is a big difference in the values of $\Delta H_{\text{hyd}}$ for $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\text{Cu}^{2+}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Calcium can be produced by the electrolysis of molten calcium chloride, $\text{CaCl}_2\text{(l)}$.

Calculate the mass, in g, of $\text{Ca}$ formed when a current of $0.75\text{A}$ passes through $\text{CaCl}_2\text{(l)}$ for 60 minutes.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
(d)
parts.text:
The reaction between A and B is feasible at low temperatures but is **not** feasible at high temperatures.

$$\text{A} + \text{B} \rightleftharpoons \text{C} + \text{D}$$

Deduce the signs of $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ for this reaction and explain why the feasibility changes with temperature.
